items.title: Impl selectors: an ABSOLUTE-PATH subject (`(impl pkg::lib::overlay::Overlay)`, `(impl std::web::style::Style)`) resolves from the root anywhere a path stands in the subject type - tuple elements, generic arguments, array elements, closure types - independent of the importing file's scope (today: '`pkg` is a namespace, not a value'); and the bare one-selector form `m::(impl T)` beside `m::{ (impl T) }`, canonicalized by fmt as a one-member set is
items.status: OPEN - RULED 2026-11-03 by the owner (part A option 4 accepted; the bare form and non-identifier subjects asked - answered in the reply, built as the item says); Order 56's parser/solver lane
items.discussion: the owner 2026-11-03 ran into 'the subject must already be in the importing file's scope' (a selector `(impl Overlay)` in a file that does not import Overlay fails with cannot-find-type); experiments on a kolt copy under next: the module-qualified subject `(impl overlay::Overlay)` after `import pkg::lib::overlay;` WORKS (the spec's 'qualified spelling'), the absolute `(impl pkg::lib::overlay::Overlay)` is refused (`pkg` is a namespace, not a value - the subject parser reads it as a value path). B688's quick-fix (E359) needs a spelling it can emit without reading the file's imports
items.body: (1) The subject of a selector is a TYPE; resolve paths inside it with root paths allowed (`pkg::` / `std::` heads resolve as import paths do), in the type resolver rather than at the subject's head - so `(impl (pkg::d::T, std::e::U))`, `(impl List<pkg::d::T>)`, `(impl [std::e::U; _])` and a closure type all take absolute paths in every position; the bare-name rule (resolved in the importing file's scope) and the module-qualified rule stay. (2) The bare form `import m::(impl T);` and `import m::(impl T)::first;` as the one-selector spelling, exactly as `import a::b;` is the one-name spelling of `import a::{ b };`; the formatter canonicalizes a one-selector set to it (formatter.rs ~:5870's rule for a one-member set), so braces appear only with two or more members. (3) E359's quick-fix then emits `import {module}::(impl {absolute subject});`. Pins: each subject position with an absolute path, red before; the bare form parses, formats, round-trips; the module-qualified and bare-name rules unchanged; the estate's existing selectors unchanged (kolt writes `(impl Overlay)`, `(impl bool with Display)`). Spec names.md §4.3. Sizing S-M.

items.title: A plain import admits the LEAF module's impl blocks only, never a parent directory's (part B, 'B1-leaf'): a directory body's blocks arrive through a prelude or an explicit import of that directory, so nothing implicit can be dropped by adding a selector; and the package PRELUDE blessed as the place to admit a package's extension blocks once
items.kind: language (imports; M; BREAKING for files that leaned on directory-body impls)
items.status: OPEN - RULED 2026-11-03 by the owner (part B: B1 accepted in the leaf shape); Order 56's parser/solver lane after A181, a paper slice first (visibility.md §12)
items.discussion: the owner 2026-11-03 leaned to 'block impls are required, always; bless preludes harder'; the integrator's leaf shape keeps the common case one line (`import std::display::Display;` still admits std::display's own `impl List<T: Display>`) while removing the action at a distance of names.md §4.1 ('an extension impl written in a directory's body arrives in any file that imports a module beneath it') and the refactor trap (adding a selector to a plain statement silently drops the path impls it carried - today's 'these implementations only'); the owner accepted. B2 (a selector only adds) declined
items.body: (1) names.md §4.1/§4.3: a plain `import a::b::c;` admits the blocks declared in `c`'s file (and a selector narrows them); `a`'s and `a::b`'s directory-body blocks are admitted only by an import that names them (`import a::b;`, `import a::b::{ (impl _) };`) or by a prelude. `only` keeps its meaning. (2) The package prelude (vilan.toml `prelude = ...` today names a std module) may name a PACKAGE module, whose `export import ...::{ (impl T) };` re-exports admit blocks to every file of the package - kolt writes its 64 overlay admissions once. (3) Estate census first (the paper slice): every file of std, the website, the corpus, the docs fences and kolt that calls a method arriving only through a directory body - fix std/corpus/docs, report website and kolt (the owner's patch; with (2) likely one line). CHANGELOG `breaking`. Pins: a directory-body block no longer reaches a child's importer; the explicit import does; the prelude does; adding a selector to a plain statement drops nothing it did not name. Sizing M.
